description: Shared reading rules (29-EVENT-CENTRED-INQUIRY.md §7): what the reader is told in every inquiry, so the rules cannot drift between inquiries. The reader's guidance is composed from these rules, the source's brief (discovery/source_brief.py), and whatever an inquiry adds that is particular to it. Like the predicate registry, nothing here names a source or a subject; nothing points at a passage or quotes a source.
general: Give a time marker in the source's own words as the time expression. Add time_edtf only when the passage states the year.
Notes by a modern editor, translator, or transcriber, and an author's footnotes, are never the author's text.

Where the author reads an event as an instance of an in-scope concept, draft exemplifies; where the author presents a long-range consequence of it, draft ledTo. Record any other reading of what the events meant as a note of type interpretation.
eventInquiry: This inquiry is the event itself, not any one book. Read each source for the steps of the event as that source tells them: the decisions and movements that lead into it, the action itself, and what ends it, when the source ties them to the event. Each step is a depicted event of this source.
A fleet, a wing or the centre of a fleet, a squadron, or a land army in scope can take part in a depicted event as a participant, as a person can.
Order the steps only where the source orders them: by a time marker, by saying one followed another, or by presenting one as the cause or outcome of another.

predicates.participatedIn: For participatedIn in the narrative event as a whole, a person counts as taking part when the passage shows them present during it: commanding, fighting, aboard a ship in the action, or fleeing from it. Preparations before the event, or the actions of a person's ships or troops with no sign of the person, do not by themselves show that the person took part.
predicates.commanded: commanded relates a person to a force they directed in action, using the force entities in scope: a fleet, one wing or the centre of a fleet, a squadron, or a land army. Command of a wing or the centre is not command of the whole fleet; use the most specific force the passage supports.
predicates.heldAuthorityOver: heldAuthorityOver is formal or supreme authority over a force, whether or not the person directed it in the fighting, for example an overall commander whose subordinate leads a wing. Draft it when the passage shows that authority, with a time only if the passage gives one.

reference: This is a reference work written by many contributors: a summary of other sources, read at one revision. Draft as claims what the work itself states.
Where the work reports what a named ancient or modern author says, the claim is still the work's account: say in the rationale whose account it reports.

scope.description: An event inquiry's scope, computed from the graph instead of declared: the event's neighbours through live claims; the entities of these kinds that take part in the event's parts (events partOf it); the command structure of what is then in scope; every Concept; and, with scopeFromMentions, the entities its sources' passages mention. Depicted events stay out (the reader sees its own source's list).
